title: Close photo-manifest secret redaction
verify: Independent security verification injects the shared corpus through actual manifest serialization, observes redaction/rejection before atomic write, proves safe failure cleanup, and confirms source values are unchanged.
evidence_required: FT-015-AC-007 RED/GREEN: inject the configured corpus through the actual manifest writer; RED is any raw secret written or lack of decisive pre-write rejection, GREEN is sanitized/blocked output before atomic rename with no accepted unsafe manifest and unchanged source credential; decisive comparison: parsed file/failure artifacts and source value; artifact: focused transcript under .tasks/TASK-067-T3-FT-015-W2/. Preserve exact pre-implementation GREEN if already satisfied.
purpose: Make the accepted photo manifest an explicitly safe product output without changing Photo Catalog/artifact authority.
success_outcome: Actual manifest serialization removes or rejects all configured secret/auth values before atomic persistence; sanitizer/write failure leaves no accepted unsafe manifest and existing cleanup/Photo Intake behavior remains intact.
anti_goals: Do not change manifest schema, photo identity/layout, upload limits, catalog persistence, Timeline/Dataset behavior, or source credentials.
Do not adopt log/error or other output-owner ACs.
constraints: Apply sanitization before bytes reach the atomic writer; never clean up after acceptance as proof.
Preserve strict allowed manifest shape and existing rollback cleanup.
invariants: Accepted manifests contain no forbidden corpus.
Redaction does not mutate authentication/provider source values or grant artifact/runtime authority.
verification_targets: FT-015-AC-007: actual writer RED/GREEN or preserved pre-GREEN, safe failure/cleanup, parsed manifest corpus absence, and source integrity.

forbidden_scope: Manifest schema expansion, Photo Catalog migration, Timeline/history, Bus/UI, agent runtime, frontend, or sync.
stop_conditions: Safety requires changing the accepted manifest schema/product fields.
The writer cannot fail safely without altering upload transaction semantics beyond this AC.
